newsitem.title: USA: Southeastern Michigan Gas to take charge.
newsitem.headline: Southeastern Michigan Gas to take charge.

text.p: Southeastern Michigan Gas Enterprises Inc said Thursday it will take a one-time, non-cash after tax charge against earnings of $21 million in the fourth quarter.
The charge is for writing down its investment and participation in NOARK Pipeline System LP, in which Southeastern Michigan holds a 32 percent general partnership interest.
Southeastern Michigan said the charge, on a pre-tax basis, represents a significant portion of its current investment, including loan guarantees, in the 302-mile gas pipeline.
NOARK extends from Ft. Chaffee, Ark., across the northern part of the state. The pipeline was built in 1991-92 at a cost of $103 million.

"Relieving the company of the drag on its earnings and stock price caused by the NOARK operation has been one of my primary goals since I joined the company in May of last year," William Johnson, president, said in a statement.
Johnson added that, after the charge is taken to write down the investment, Southeastern Michigan expects to see a positive impact on earnings of $0.14 a share on an annual basis.
Robert Caldwell, chief financial officer, said the positive impact to earnings will begin in 1997.

"The investment community has been very concerned about our investment since the pipeline began operating at a loss in 1992," Johnson said. "We believe our stock price is undervalued, due to the negative impact of NOARK."
Southeastern Michigan shares were up 3/8 at 19-1/4.

Southeastern said it will continue to explore opportunities to improve NOARK, but the write-down will eliminate the need for significant NOARK operating losses to be recorded on future income statements.
The company said it continues to try to sell its interest in NOARK.
The NOARK partnership also includes Southwestern Energy Co as operator and general partner with a 48 percent interest and The Prudential Insurance Co, the primary lender with a 20 percent interest.
